rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone gets through a dangerous, painful, or traumatic event or period.

example.english: Luckily, they survive that serious crash.
example.traditional: 嗰場車禍咁嚴重，好彩佢捱過咗。
example.jyutping: go2 coeng4 ce1 wo6 gam3 jim4 zung6 hou2 coi2 keoi5 ngaai4 gwo3 zo2

rows.note: Use this when the focus is that a person stays alive after a life-threatening situation.

example.english: Even after falling from such a height, they survive.
example.traditional: 咁高處跌落嚟，佢都保住條命。
example.jyutping: gam3 gou1 cyu3 dit3 lok6 lai4 keoi5 dou1 bou2 zyu6 tiu4 meng6

rows.note: Use this conversational expression for a person, thing, or idea that is still around or still exists.

example.english: That old shop continues to survive after all these years.
example.jyutping: gam3 do1 nin4 gaan1 lou5 pou2 zung6 hai2 dou6

rows.note: Use this comparative expression when someone lives longer than another person or something lasts longer than another thing.

example.english: This old car will survive longer than that new one.
example.traditional: 呢架舊車長命過嗰架新車。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaa3 gau6 ce1 coeng4 meng6 gwo3 go2 gaa3 san1 ce1
